en: The Bhikṣuṇī-Prātimokṣa Sūtra of the Mūlasarvāstivāda,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing by Imperial Decree:
"The Prātimokṣa Sūtra is difficult to hear, even after the passage of immeasurable koṭis of kalpas."
Reciting, studying, and upholding [the teachings] is likewise so; those who practice as they have been taught are even rarer to encounter.
It is a joy for the Buddhas to appear in the world; it is a joy to proclaim the subtle and sublime True Dharma.
It is a joy for the Saṃgha to be of one mind and a single vision; it is a joy to practice together in harmony with courageous diligence.
To see the noble ones is joy, and to dwell together with them is likewise joy;
not seeing those who are foolish and deluded—this is what is called constantly experiencing happiness.
To see one who is endowed with ethical discipline is joy; to see one who is learned is also called joy;
to see an Arhat is true joy, because of the non-arising of further existence.
There is joy in the delightful stairway at the river crossing; there is joy in conquering enemies through the Dharma.
When the fruit of right wisdom is realized, there is the joy of being able to eliminate the conceit of "I am" entirely.
If one can form a resolute intention, well-subduing the senses and desires while possessing great learning;
from youth until old age dwelling in the forest, one finds joy in the tranquility and seclusion of the araṇya.
"Venerable sirs!

So much of the spring season has passed, and so much remains. Since old age and death have already encroached, our life-force gradually diminishes; the Great Teacher’s Dharma will soon be extinguished."
"Venerable sirs!
You should strive to manifest [the Dharma] and not be negligent.
Through non-negligence, you will certainly realize the state of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha; how much more so the other wholesome dharmas belonging to enlightenment!"
"Venerable Saṃgha! What should be done first?
The Buddha’s community of śrāvakas seeks little and has few concerns."
"Those who have not yet received full ordination must depart.
Those bhikṣuṇīs who are absent shall announce their *chanda* (consent) and *viśuddhi* (purity). Those who hold the *chanda* shall each speak before those seated in pairs.
With palms joined in reverence, pay homage to the Lion of the Śākyas.
I shall speak of the Prātimokṣa discipline; listen well, O virtuous ones.
Having heard it, you should practice correctly as taught by the Great Sage;
even regarding minor offenses, guard yourselves with courage and diligence.
The horse of the mind is difficult to restrain; it must be governed by constant courage and resolve.
The Prātimokṣa is like a bridle, equipped with a hundred extremely sharp pins.
If a person violates the rules of conduct, they can stop immediately upon hearing the instruction.
The Great Being is like a fine horse; he shall emerge from the battle array of afflictions.
If a person lacks this bridle, they will never find joy;
submerged in the battle array of afflictions, they wander deluded through birth and death.
"Listen, Venerable Bhikṣuṇī Saṃgha!
Today is the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight—or as it is said:
'the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight'—of the Saṃgha."
"Let the Poṣadha be performed.
If the Bhikṣuṇī Saṃgha is ready and gives its consent, may the Bhikṣuṇī Saṃgha permit that the Bhikṣuṇī Saṃgha now perform the Poṣadha and recite the Prātimokṣa Sūtra."
"Thus it is declared. "Venerable sirs!
I shall now perform the poṣadha and recite the Prātimokṣa Sūtra."
Venerable sirs, listen attentively and reflect well upon this. Those who have committed an offense should confess it; those who have committed no offense should remain silent.
By remaining silent, it shall be known that the venerable ones are pure.
Just as you would answer truthfully when questioned at other times, so too, within this assembly of superior bhikṣuṇīs, you should answer truthfully even up to three times being asked.
If a bhikṣuṇī remembers having committed an offense and does not disclose it, she incurs the offense of intentional lying.
Venerable sirs, the Buddha has declared that intentional lying is an obstructive dharma; therefore, a bhikṣuṇī who seeks purity must disclose it.
"To disclose [one's transgressions] brings peace and happiness; not to disclose them brings no peace or happiness.
"Venerable sirs, I have recited the introduction to the Prātimokṣa Sūtra."
Now I ask the venerable ones:
"Are you pure in this matter?
Thus he asks three times: "Venerable ones!"
"In this matter, we are pure, as indicated by our silence; thus do I now hold it.
"Venerable sirs!
These eight *pārājika* rules are recited every half-month within the *Prātimokṣa-sūtra*."
The summary verse says:
Impurity, taking what is not given, claiming superhuman states, touching the eight things, concealing, and following [a schism]; for these, there is no communal living.

"If again a bhikṣuṇī, having received the training rules together with other bhikṣuṇīs, does not relinquish the training rules and, while her training is weak, does not declare it herself, commits the act of impurity—the method of sexual intercourse—even with an animal, this bhikṣuṇī also incurs a pārājika offense and should not live in community."
"Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī, whether in a village or in a secluded place, takes with a thieving mind an object not given by another;
and while she is thus stealing, if a king or a minister should seize her, or kill her, or bind her, or banish her, or reprimand her, saying:
'Hey, woman!'"
"You are a thief, foolish and ignorant, to commit such a theft.
If a bhikṣuṇī steals in this manner, she too incurs a pārājika offense and shall not live in community with the others.

"Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī intentionally takes the life of a human being or a human fetus with her own hand, or provides a weapon, or wields a weapon herself, or seeks out one who wields a weapon, or encourages death, or praises death, saying: 'O woman!'"
"What use is this burdened, impure, and evil life?
You would be better off dead now; death is superior to life.
Thus, according to his own thoughts, he uses various words to exhort and praise [the victim], urging them toward death.
If that person dies because of it, this bhikṣuṇī also incurs a pārājika offense and shall not live in communal residence with the Saṃgha.

"Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī, while actually lacking knowledge and universal knowledge, and knowing for herself that she has not attained the superhuman state—the peaceful, noble, and sublime realization, wisdom, vision, and dwelling in bliss—yet says, 'I know; I see.'"
At another time, whether questioned or unasked, desiring to purify himself, he speaks thus:
"Venerable sirs!
It is true that I neither knew nor saw, yet I said I knew and I said I saw; this was a false and deceptive lie."
"Except in the case of overweening pride (*adhimāna*), this bhikṣuṇī also incurs a *pārājika* offense and should not live in community.

Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī, with a lustful mind, together with a man who has a lustful mind, from below her armpits to above her knees, acts with the intent to experience pleasure by rubbing or excessively rubbing her body against his, for such an act, this bhikṣuṇī also incurs a *pārājika* offense and should not live in community."

"Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī, with a lustful mind, together with a man who has a lustful mind, engages in flirtatious laughter; indicates a place; makes a sign at the appointed time; comes and goes to the man; consents to each other's intentions; lies down with her body extended in a place where such conduct is improper; and thus mutually accepts these eight matters—[she commits an offense]."
If a bhikṣuṇī performs such an act, she also incurs a pārājika offense and shall not live in community.
Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī, having previously known that another bhikṣuṇī has committed a defeat (pārājika) offense, does not disclose it.
After that person has died, or has returned to lay life, or has departed, they should then speak these words:
"The community of nuns should know that I previously knew this bhikṣuṇī had committed a pārājika offense regarding such-and-such a matter."
This bhikṣuṇī also commits a pārājika offense and should not live in communion.

Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī knows that the Saṃgha of bhikṣus has performed the *sthāpanīya-karman* (act of suspension) against a certain bhikṣu, and the community of bhikṣuṇīs likewise performs the *anavaśrāvaṇīya-dharma* (the rule of non-prostration) against him; [if she acts thus, she also commits a pārājika offense].
That bhikṣu, manifesting an appearance of reverence toward the Saṃgha and seeking deliverance, personally requested within the boundary the lifting of the *sthāpanīya-karman* (the act of suspension).
That bhikṣuṇī replied to the bhikṣu, saying:
"Noble One!..."
Do not manifest an appearance of reverence toward the Saṃgha out of a desire for deliverance, nor seek within the boundary the lifting of the *sthāpanīya-karman* (the act of suspension).
I shall provide the Venerable One with robes, alms-bowls, and other requisites so that nothing is lacking; you may then settle your mind in recitation and mental cultivation.
Then the bhikṣuṇīs said to this bhikṣuṇī:
"Do you not know that the Saṃgha has performed the *pratisāraṇīya-karman* against this person, and that we bhikṣuṇīs have imposed upon him the rule of non-prostration?"
That bhikṣu, having aroused a humble mind, shall himself request within the boundary the formal act of suspension (niśraya-vinaya).
You should then provide him with robes, alms bowls, and other requisites, ensuring he lacks for nothing.
"You should now abandon this compliance with [the laity].
When the bhikṣuṇīs have admonished her in this manner, it is well if she abandons it;
if she does not abandon it, they should admonish her earnestly and correctly up to three times, and following their instruction, they should reprove her so as to cause her to abandon this matter.
"If she renounces it, that is well;
if she does not renounce it, this bhikṣuṇī also incurs a pārājika offense and shall not be lived with.
"Venerable sirs!"
I have already explained the eight *pārājika* rules; if a bhikṣuṇī commits any one of these offenses, she may no longer dwell together with the other bhikṣuṇīs.
As it was before, so it is after: having incurred a *pārājika* offense, she should not live in communal residence.
Now I ask the venerable ones:
"Are you pure in this matter?
Thus he asks three times: "Venerable ones!"
"Since we are pure in this matter and remain silent, I now hold it to be so.
"Venerable sirs!
These twenty *saṃghāvaśeṣa* rules are recited in the *Prātimokṣa Sūtra* every half-month."
The summary verse says:
Matchmaking and the two types of slander, The two defilements and the four solitary acts,
A husband’s abandonment, the dissolution of agreements, The two disputes, the mixed [residence], and living alone.
Schism in the Saṃgha and its followers, Defiling families and being of evil character;
The formal acts of the community number twenty, Of which eight involve three admonitions—one should know.

"If again a bhikṣuṇī acts as a matchmaker, conveying a man’s intent to a woman and a woman’s intent to a man, whether for the purpose of marriage or for illicit intercourse, even for a mere moment, it is a *saṃghāvaśeṣa*."
"If again a bhikṣuṇī, out of malice and without relinquishing it, should defame a pure bhikṣuṇī with a groundless *pārājika* offense, desiring to ruin her pure conduct."
At a later time, whether questioned or unasked, if it is known that this was groundless slander,
and that the bhikṣuṇī spoke these words out of malice, it is a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense.
"If again a bhikṣuṇī, out of malice and without relinquishing it, should defame a pure bhikṣuṇī with a groundless *pārājika* offense, desiring to ruin her pure conduct."
Later, at another time, whether questioned or unasked, knowing this to be a matter that is extraneous and improper, one slanders [another] by means of a slight resemblance of dharma.
If that bhikṣuṇī utters such words out of malice, it is a saṃghāvaśeṣa.
Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī, with a lustful mind, receives anything whatsoever from a man with a lustful mind, it is a saṃghāvaśeṣa.
"If again a bhikṣuṇī should speak thus to another bhikṣuṇī:
'If you, being free from a defiled mind, accept goods from a man with a defiled mind, what fault is there on my part?'"
...this constitutes a *saṃghāvaśeṣa*.
Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī stays overnight alone in another place after departing from a nunnery, it is a *saṃghāvaśeṣa*.
"If a bhikṣuṇī again goes alone from a nunnery during the day to a layperson's home, it is a saṃghāvaśeṣa.
If a bhikṣuṇī again travels alone on a road, it is a saṃghāvaśeṣa."
"If a bhikṣuṇī again swims across a river alone, it is a saṃghāvaśeṣa.

"If a bhikṣuṇī again, knowing that another woman has committed an unlawful act, is universally despised by the people, has been abandoned by her husband, and has even informed the king, yet ordains her to leave the household life, it is a saṃghāvaśeṣa."
"If a bhikṣuṇī, relying on an old agreement with others, seeks for herself the property of a deceased person, it is a saṃghāvaśeṣa.

"If a bhikṣuṇī, knowing that a bhikṣuṇī has been subjected by the community of bhikṣuṇīs to the formal act of *pratisaṃharaṇīya-karman* (the act of suspension), should go outside the boundary to perform the rite of its revocation, it is a saṃghāvaśeṣa."
"If, moreover, a bhikṣuṇī, having engaged in quarreling and strife with other bhikṣuṇīs, should speak thus:
'I renounce the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha.

It is not only these śramaṇa daughters of the Śākyas who possess the precepts, possess virtue, and possess superior wholesome dharmas; other śramaṇas also possess the precepts, possess virtue, and possess superior wholesome dharmas. I shall go to them to practice the holy life.'"
Then the bhikṣuṇīs said to her:
"You should relinquish this sinful and evil view.
When she was thus exhorted, if she relinquished it, that was well.
If he does not relinquish it, one should admonish him earnestly and correctly two or three times, and should reprove him according to the instruction, so that he may relinquish this matter.
If he relinquishes it, it is well;
if he does not relinquish it, it is a *saṃghāvaśeṣa*.
"If, moreover, a bhikṣuṇī is engaged in quarreling and turmoil with other bhikṣuṇīs, and those bhikṣuṇīs say to that bhikṣuṇī: 'Sister!'"
"Do not engage in quarrels or disturbances.
If that bhikṣuṇī speaks thus:
"You possess attachment, aversion, fear, and delusion; therefore, you either obstruct or do not obstruct those who are quarreling."
The bhikṣuṇīs said to her:
"Venerable lady!
When others are admonishing and instructing you, do not speak in this manner."
"You possess love, hatred, fear, and delusion; therefore, regarding those who engage in quarrels, you may either obstruct them or not.
"Sister, please desist from such speech!
When the bhikṣuṇīs have offered this admonition, it is well if she abandons [the behavior].
If he does not relinquish it, one should admonish him earnestly and formally up to two or three times, and according to the instruction, one should reprove him so that he may relinquish this matter.
If he relinquishes it, it is well;
if he does not relinquish it, it is a *saṃghāvaśeṣa*.
"If, furthermore, a bhikṣuṇī lives in disorderly association with other bhikṣuṇīs, being restless and engaging in frivolous laughter,
and the other bhikṣuṇīs say to that bhikṣuṇī: 'Sister!'"
Do not dwell in disorder or engage in agitation and frivolous laughter.
When you dwell in disorder, it causes wholesome qualities to decline and prevents them from increasing; therefore, you should dwell separately.
"When living apart, it will cause wholesome dharmas to increase and prevent them from further declining.
When the bhikṣuṇīs have admonished her in this manner, it is well if she relinquishes [the matter];
if she does not relinquish it, they should admonish her earnestly and correctly up to three times, following the instruction by interrogating her, so that she may relinquish this matter.
"If she abandons it, it is well;
if she does not abandon it, it is a *saṃghāvaśeṣa*.
Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī knows that another bhikṣuṇī desires to live alone..."
The bhikṣuṇīs said to that bhikṣuṇī:
"Venerable one!
Do not dwell alone; when you dwell alone, it causes wholesome dharmas to decline and prevents them from increasing."
Sisters! You should dwell together so that wholesome qualities may increase and no longer decline.
The bhikṣuṇīs should also say to her:
"Venerable one,
do not take pleasure in dwelling alone, for it causes the wholesome dharmas to decline."
"Venerable one!
You ought to abandon this solitary and evil view.
When he is thus admonished, it is well if he abandons it;
If he does not relinquish it, one should admonish him earnestly and correctly two or three times, and should question him in accordance with the instruction, so that he may relinquish this matter.
If he relinquishes it, it is well;
if he does not relinquish it, it is a *saṃghāvaśeṣa*.
"If, moreover, a bhikṣuṇī should employ means with the intent to cause a schism in a harmonious Saṃgha, and should persistently cling to that act of schism without relinquishing it,
the other bhikṣuṇīs should say to that bhikṣuṇī: 'Sister!'"
Do not persist in your stubborn adherence with the desire to cause a schism in the Saṃgha. Sisters!

You should live in harmony with the Saṃgha, dwelling together in joy and without dispute; being of one mind and one voice, like water mixed with milk, you shall cause the Teacher’s dispensation to shine forth and endure for a long time in peace and happiness.
"Venerable lady!
You should relinquish this act of causing a schism in the Saṃgha.
When the bhikṣuṇīs have admonished her in this manner, it is well if she relinquishes it.
If he does not relinquish it, he should be earnestly and formally admonished up to three times, and questioned according to the instruction, so that he may relinquish this matter.
If he relinquishes it, it is well;
if he does not relinquish it, it is a *saṃghāvaśeṣa*.
"If, furthermore, a bhikṣuṇī—whether one, two, or many—forms a faction with another bhikṣuṇī, adhering to and dwelling in accordance with that which is heterodox and contrary to the Dharma."
Then that bhikṣuṇī said to the other bhikṣuṇīs:
"Venerable ladies!
Do not engage in any discussion with that bhikṣuṇī, whether it be about her good qualities or her faults."
Why is this? Because that bhikṣuṇī conforms to the Dharma and Vinaya and relies upon the Dharma and Vinaya; her speech is not false. What she loves and delights in, I too love and delight in.
The bhikṣuṇīs should say to this bhikṣuṇī:
"Venerable one!
Do not speak in this way."
"That bhikṣuṇī conforms to the Dharma and the Vinaya, and relies upon the Dharma and the Vinaya; her speech is not false. What she finds delightful, I also find delightful. Why is this?"

That bhikṣuṇī does not conform to the Dharma and Vinaya, nor does she rely upon the Dharma and Vinaya; her words are entirely false. You must not delight in causing a schism in the Saṃgha; you should instead delight in the harmony of the Saṃgha.

One should live in harmony with the Saṃgha, joyful and without dispute, with a single mind and a single teaching, like water and milk blending together, so that the Great Teacher’s instruction may be made radiant and endure for a long time in peace and happiness.
"Venerable lady!
You should abandon this evil view of schisming the Saṃgha, which follows what is false and opposes what is right, and cease from persistently maintaining this contentious matter.
When the bhikṣuṇīs have admonished her in this way, it is well if she abandons it; [if she does not, she commits a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense].
If he does not relinquish it, he should be earnestly and formally admonished two or three times, and questioned in accordance with the instruction, so that he may relinquish this matter.
If he relinquishes it, it is well;
if he does not relinquish it, it is a *saṃghāvaśeṣa*.

"Furthermore, if many bhikṣuṇīs reside in a village or town and defile the families of others and engage in evil conduct—such that their defiling of families is seen, heard, and known by the public, and their engagement in evil conduct is also seen, heard, and known by the public."
The bhikṣuṇīs should say to those bhikṣuṇīs:
"Venerable ladies!

You have defiled families and committed evil deeds; that you have defiled families is known by the community through seeing and hearing, and that you have committed evil deeds is also known by the community through seeing and hearing."
"You all may go; you should not remain here.
Those bhikṣuṇīs said to the other bhikṣuṇīs:
"The Venerable Ones possess favoritism, hatred, fear, and delusion, for there are bhikṣuṇīs who have committed the same offense, yet some are expelled while others are not."
Then the bhikṣuṇīs said to that bhikṣuṇī:
"Venerable one!
Do not speak such words."
"Venerable sirs, there are [among you] those who possess affection, hatred, fear, and delusion; for there are bhikṣuṇīs guilty of the same offense, some of whom are expelled and others who are not."
Why is this? Because these bhikṣuṇīs are free from attachment, aversion, fear, and delusion.

You, however, have defiled families and committed evil deeds; that you have defiled families is known by the community through seeing, hearing, and awareness, and that you have committed evil deeds is likewise known by the community through seeing, hearing, and awareness.
"Venerable ladies!
You should abandon such speech as 'love' and 'hatred.
When the bhikṣuṇīs have been admonished in this way, it is well if they abandon it."

If they do not relinquish it, one should earnestly and formally admonish them two or three times, and according to the instruction, one should reprove them, so as to cause them to relinquish this matter.
If they relinquish it, that is well; if not...
"If she does not relinquish [this attitude], it is a *saṃghāvaśeṣa*.

Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī is of an evil nature and refuses to accept the words of others, and when the bhikṣuṇīs, in accordance with the Dharma and the Vinaya, offer her admonition regarding the *Prātimokṣa* Sūtra spoken by the Buddha, she does not accept their counsel, saying:
'Venerable ladies!'"
Do not speak to me even a little, whether good or bad; nor shall I speak to the venerable ones, whether good or bad.
Venerable ones, please stop!
"Do not exhort me; do not speak ill of me.
The bhikṣuṇīs said to that bhikṣuṇī, "Venerable one!"

Do not refuse to accept admonition; when the bhikṣuṇīs offer you counsel in accordance with the Dharma and the Vinaya from within the Bhikṣuṇī Prātimokṣa Sūtra as spoken by the Buddha, you should accept their admonition.

Venerable one, when you admonish the bhikṣuṇīs in accordance with the Dharma, and the bhikṣuṇīs likewise admonish you in accordance with the Dharma, in this way the Saṅgha of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha—the disciples of the Buddha—shall flourish through mutual admonition and instruction.
"Venerable ladies!
You should relinquish this matter.
When the bhikṣuṇīs have been admonished in this way, it is well if they relinquish it; [if not, they should be dealt with according to the rule].

If he does not relinquish it, one should admonish him earnestly and correctly two or three times, and should question him in accordance with the instruction, so as to cause him to relinquish this matter.
If he relinquishes it, that is well;
if he does not relinquish it, it is a *saṃghāvaśeṣa*.
"Venerable sirs!
I have now recited the twenty *saṃghāvaśeṣa* dharmas: twelve are offenses upon first commission, and eight require up to three admonitions.
If a bhikṣuṇī conceals any one of these offenses she has committed, the two-fold *saṃgha* shall grant her the *mānatva* penance for half a month."

When the *mānatva* penance has been completed, there remains the matter of the removal of the offense (*āpattivyutthāna*). If it is deemed acceptable by both Sanghas, then within an assembly of forty members—consisting of twenty members from each of the two Sanghas—the offense of this bhikṣuṇī shall be removed.
If there is one person missing such that the assembly does not reach forty, this bhikṣuṇī’s offense cannot be cleared, and the Saṃghas of both divisions incur an offense.
This is the method for the removal of the offense.
Now I ask the venerable ones:
"Are you pure in this matter?
Thus he asks three times: "Venerable ones!"
"In this matter, we are pure, as indicated by our silence; thus do I hold it.
Regarding the two *aniyata* rules for bhikṣuṇīs: "Venerable sirs!
These thirty-three *naiḥsargika-pāyattika* rules are recited every half-month within the Prātimokṣa Sūtra."
The initial summary verse says:
Holding, separating, keeping, and washing robes; Taking robes, begging, and receiving excess;
Equal value and different owners; Sending a messenger to deliver the price for robes.
"Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī has finished making her robes and the kaṭhina cloth is subsequently spread out, she may keep an extra robe for up to ten days without having to distribute it."
If one keeps [the robe] beyond that limit, it is a *naiḥsargika-pāyattika*.

Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī has finished making her robes and the *kaṭhina* period has expired, and she stays overnight—even for a single night—outside the boundary separated from any one of her five robes, except when authorized by the community, it is a *naiḥsargika-pāyattika*.

"Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī has finished making her robes and the kaṭhina robe has been suspended, and she obtains an out-of-season robe, she may accept it if she has need of it; having accepted it, she must quickly have it made into a robe."
If there is a source from which one expects to obtain [an item] to satisfy a need, and it has not yet been obtained, one may keep it for up to one month.
If this period is exceeded, it is a *naiḥsargika-pāyattika* offense.
"If a bhikṣuṇī should wash, dye, or beat a used garment for a bhikṣu who is not a relative, it is a naiḥsargika-pāyattika.
If a bhikṣuṇī should receive a garment from a bhikṣu who is not a relative, except in exchange, it is a naiḥsargika-pāyattika."
"If a bhikṣuṇī should beg for a robe from a householder or a housewife who is not a relative, except at the appropriate time, it is an *naiḥsargika-pāyattika*."
As for "other times": if a bhikṣuṇī’s robe has been snatched away, lost, burned, blown away, or carried off by water—this is such a time.
Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī, whose robe has been snatched away, lost, burned, blown away, or carried off by water, should beg for a robe from a householder or a housewife who is not a relative.
If that person offers many robes and a bhikṣuṇī requires them, she should accept two robes, one for the upper body and one for the lower body.
If she accepts more than this, it is a naiḥsargika-pāyattika offense.

"If, moreover, a bhikṣuṇī should have a householder or a householder’s wife who is not a relative provide the price for a robe, intending: 'One should purchase such a pure robe and give it to a certain bhikṣuṇī for her immediate use.'"
This bhikṣuṇī, having not previously received an invitation, was informed by another and went to that person's house, saying:
"Excellent, worthy sir!
For the sake of the price for robes prepared for me, you should purchase such pure robes and give them to me in a timely manner, so that they may be of good quality."
If she should obtain the robe, it is a *naiḥsargika-pāyattika*.
Furthermore, if a monk or nun has a non-relative householder or housewife who each prepares the price for a robe, intending to buy such a pure robe and give it to a certain monk or nun.
This bhikṣuṇī, having not previously received an invitation, upon being informed by another, went to that person's house and spoke these words:
"Excellent, worthy sir!
For the sake of the robe-fund prepared for me, you may purchase such a pure robe with it and give it to me in a timely manner, so that it may be of good quality."
If she obtains the robe, it is a *naiḥsargika-pāyattika*.
Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī has a messenger sent by a king, a high minister, a brāhmaṇa, a layperson, or others, to deliver the price for a robe to her;
That messenger, taking the price for the robes, went to the bhikṣuṇī’s place and said:
"Noble Lady! These goods were sent by such-and-such a king, minister, brahmin, or householder; out of compassion, Noble Lady, please accept them."
The bhikṣuṇī said to that messenger:
"Venerable sir, I should not accept this price for a robe; if I obtain a pure robe appropriate for the season, then I shall accept it.
The messenger replied:
"Noble One! Is there an attendant?
The bhikṣuṇī who required robes replied:
"There are. Whether it be a monastery attendant (*śrāmaṇera*) or a female lay devotee (*upāsikā*), these are the attendants for the bhikṣuṇīs.
Having been told this, the messenger goes to the attendant and, after giving him the price for the robe, says:
"You may take this price for robes and purchase a timely, pure robe to give to the bhikṣuṇī so-and-so, so that she may wear it.
After that messenger has properly instructed the attendant, he returns to the bhikṣuṇī and says:
"Noble Lady!"
"The person in charge you indicated, I have already provided with the price for robes; he shall receive pure robes.
When a bhikṣuṇī requires robes, she should go to the person in charge and, after reminding him two or three times, say:

"If he succeeds, it is well;
if he does not succeed, he may go to that person up to four, five, or six times, remaining silently wherever he stands.

If she does not obtain the robe, yet seeks to obtain a robe beyond this [limit], it is a *naiḥsargika-pāyattika*.
If she ultimately does not obtain the robe, that bhikṣuṇī should go herself or send a trustworthy person to the place where the robe-price was sent, and announce:

The second summary verse says:
Handling gold and silver, lending and borrowing, buying and selling, bowls, begging for thread.

"Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī takes gold, silver, coins, or the like with her own hand, or instructs another to take them, it is a naiḥsargika-pāyattika."
"If a bhikṣuṇī again seeks profit through various forms of lending and borrowing, it is a naiḥsargika-pāyattika.

"If a bhikṣuṇī has a bowl that is less than five patches old and is still fit for use, yet seeks another bowl for the sake of its excellence and obtains one, it is a naiḥsargika-pāyattika."
That bhikṣuṇī should relinquish this bowl in the midst of the community; the community shall take the lowest-quality bowl and give it to that bhikṣuṇī, saying: "This bowl is returned to you.

You should not keep it as a personal possession, nor should you treat it with special distinction, nor should you give it away to others. You should use it carefully and gradually until it breaks, maintaining it throughout; this is the proper rule."
"If again a bhikṣuṇī herself begs for thread and has a weaver who is not a relative weave it into a robe, should she obtain the robe, it is a naiḥsargika-pāyattika."
"Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī, when a householder or a householder’s wife who is not a relative commissions a weaver who is not a relative to weave a robe for her,
and this bhikṣuṇī, having not previously received an invitation, conceives a contrary thought and goes to that weaver’s place,
saying: 'Do you know this?'"
"This robe is being woven for me.
Well done, weaver!
You should weave it well and comb it clean, selecting the finest fibers and beating it thoroughly."
‘I shall provide you with a small portion of alms-food, or something similar to alms-food, or even the price for food.
If a bhikṣuṇī, by giving such items to a weaver, obtains a robe, it is a *naiḥsargika-pāyattika*.

"If, moreover, a bhikṣuṇī has given a robe to another bhikṣuṇī, and at a later time, becoming vexed, angry, abusive, and harboring a mind of disdain and contempt, she either seizes it herself or instructs another to seize it, saying:
'Give me back my robe; I will not give it to you.'"
If a robe is separated from that person's body and she uses it for her own enjoyment, it is a *naiḥsargika-pāyattika*.
Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī knows that an item was given to the community and she diverts it for herself, it is a *naiḥsargika-pāyattika*.
"As the Blessed One has said:

'I permit sick bhikṣuṇīs to consume whatever medicines they require according to their needs—namely, ghee, oil, sugar, and honey—and to keep them for seven days, provided they maintain possession of them, and then consume them after they have been kept overnight.'"
If a bhikṣuṇī consumes [the medicine] after seven days have passed, it is a naiḥsargika-pāyattika.
Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī keeps an extra alms bowl for more than one night, if she keeps it longer than that, it is a naiḥsargika-pāyattika.
The third summary verse says:

Not clinging, relinquishing, and not relinquishing; begging for gold and silver, dyeing robes, five distinctions regarding the acquisition of profit, and the two prices for purchasing medicine and robes.
"If a bhikṣuṇī does not wear the five robes within the half-month [of the rainy season retreat], it is a naiḥsargika-pāyattika.
If a bhikṣuṇī discards the kaṭhina robe at an improper time, it is a naiḥsargika-pāyattika."
"If a bhikṣuṇī, when the time has come, does not relinquish the kaṭhina robe, it is a naiḥsargika-pāyattika.
If a bhikṣuṇī solicits gold or silver, it is a naiḥsargika-pāyattika."
"If a bhikṣuṇī, moreover, uses the proceeds from the sale of robes for food and drink, it is a naiḥsargika-pāyattika.
If a bhikṣuṇī, moreover, receives proceeds from the sale of separate robes and uses them for food and drink, it is a naiḥsargika-pāyattika."
"If a bhikṣuṇī, having received a gift of bedding and furniture, should use it for food, it is a naiḥsargika-pāyattika.
If a bhikṣuṇī, having received a gift for the summer retreat, should use it for food, it is a naiḥsargika-pāyattika."
"If a bhikṣuṇī should obtain property intended for many and divert it into her own possession, it is a naiḥsargika-pāyattika.
If a bhikṣuṇī should obtain property intended for the Saṃgha and divert it into her own possession, it is a naiḥsargika-pāyattika."
"If a bhikṣuṇī again buys various medicinal substances and ties them up and then unties them, or unties them and then ties them up again, it is a naiḥsargika-pāyattika."
"If a bhikṣuṇī possesses a costly heavy robe, it is a naiḥsargika-pāyattika.
If a bhikṣuṇī possesses a costly light robe, it is a naiḥsargika-pāyattika."
"Venerable sirs!
I have already recited the thirty-three *naiḥsargika-pāyattika* dharmas.

"Is there purity herein?

These one hundred and eighty *pāyattika* dharmas are recited every half-month within the *Prātimokṣa Sūtra*.
The first summary verse says:"
Slandering, causing schism, exposing [faults], speaking in unison,
speaking of offenses, claiming superhuman attainments, and disparaging others according to their kinship.
"Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī intentionally speaks falsehoods, it is a pāyattika."
"If a bhikṣuṇī, moreover, speaks disparagingly, it is a pāyattika.
If a bhikṣuṇī, moreover, speaks divisively, it is a pāyattika."

"If a bhikṣuṇī, knowing that the Saṃgha has settled a dispute in accordance with the Dharma and that the matter has already been resolved, should later raise the issue again at the place of the formal act (karmavācanā), it is a pāyattika."
"If a bhikṣuṇī should preach the Dharma to a man for more than five or six words, except when a wise woman is present, it is a pāyattika.
"If a bhikṣuṇī should recite the scriptures or teach the Dharma in the same phrases with one who has not yet received full ordination, it is a pāyattika."

"If a bhikṣuṇī, knowing that another bhikṣuṇī has committed a grave offense, should speak of it to one who has not yet received full ordination, except by formal authorization of the Saṃgha, it is a pāyattika."
"If a bhikṣuṇī, having actually attained the qualities of a superior person (*uttarimanussa-dhamma*), should speak of them to one who has not yet received full ordination, it is a *pāyattika*.
"If a bhikṣuṇī, having previously given her consent, should later say:
'O Venerable Ones!'"
If one diverts property intended for the Saṃgha to another individual based on personal intimacy or favoritism, it is a *pāyattika*.
Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī, during the fortnightly recitation of the Prātimokṣa Sūtra, should speak as follows:
"Venerable ones!
What is the use of reciting these minor and secondary rules of training? When these precepts are being recited, they cause the bhikṣuṇīs to feel remorse, distress, and regret."
"If one thus reviles and scorns the precepts, it is a *pāyattika*.
The second summary verse says:
Seeds, reviling, and instructing; laying out beds and spreading grass and leaves.
"Staying forcefully on a bed free of insects, one passes through the three places of the non-Buddhists.
Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī herself destroys a village of seeds or sentient beings, or causes another to destroy them, it is a pāyattika."
"If any bhikṣuṇī, out of malice, reviles or treats another bhikṣuṇī with contempt, it is a pāyattika.
"If any bhikṣuṇī, in opposition to a verbal instruction, causes vexation, it is a pāyattika."

"If a bhikṣuṇī places monastic bedding or various seats in an open area and, upon departing, neither puts them away herself nor instructs another to do so, and if there is no other bhikṣuṇī to whom she has entrusted them—unless there is a special reason—this is a pāyattika offense."

"If a bhikṣuṇī, within a monastic dwelling, spreads grass or leaves herself or instructs another to spread them, and upon departing neither removes them herself nor instructs another to remove them, and if there is no other bhikṣuṇī to whom she has entrusted them, except in cases of other circumstances, it is a pāyattika."

"Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī, knowing that other bhikṣuṇīs are already residing in a monastery dwelling, later arrives there and intentionally causes them distress or offense by sitting or lying down upon their bedding with the thought:
'If they experience discomfort, they will naturally avoid me and leave.'"

Pāyattika: "If, moreover, a bhikṣuṇī, in a monastery dwelling, knowing that it is an upper story or a loft with removable legs, should sit or lie down upon it by throwing herself down, it is a pāyattika."
"If a bhikṣuṇī, knowing that water contains living organisms, herself sprinkles it upon grass or soil, or mixes it with cow dung, or instructs another to do so, it is a pāyattika."
"Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī constructs a large dwelling, she should install a crossbar at the side of the door-post, as well as windows and drainage outlets."
If, when building a wall, it is made of wet mud, it should be two or three layers high at the level of the horizontal crossbars.
If it exceeds this, it is a *pāyattika*.
"Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī stays at a dwelling place of non-Buddhists for more than one night and one meal, except in cases of illness, it is a *pāyattika*."
The third summary verse says:
Eating more than three [bowlfuls], not leaving food remaining, Encouraging [others to eat] to fullness, and eating separately from the group;
Eating at improper times, touching food with unwashed hands, and not receiving [food directly]; [Seeing] insects, non-Buddhists, and inspecting one's robes.

"If, moreover, a number of bhikṣuṇīs go to the homes of laypeople, and there are faithful brahmins or householders who earnestly invite them to accept cakes, parched grain, or boiled rice, those bhikṣuṇīs who require such food should accept two or three bowls."
If one accepts more than this, it is a *pāyattika* offense.
Once the food has been accepted and one has returned to the residence, if there are bhikṣuṇīs present, they should share the meal together; this is the proper time.
"If a bhikṣuṇī, having finished her meal, eats again without performing the *kṛtapiṇḍapāta* (the ritual for leftover food), it is a *pāyattika*.
"If a bhikṣuṇī, knowing that another bhikṣuṇī has finished her meal, encourages her to eat more without performing the *kṛtapiṇḍapāta*, saying:
'Venerable one!'"
"You should eat this food.
If, for such reasons, she intends to cause another to commit an offense and thereby produce grief and distress, it is a *pāyattika*.

The exceptions are: when one is ill, when working, when traveling on a road, when traveling by boat, when a large assembly is eating, or when śramaṇas are distributing food—these are the appropriate times.
"If a bhikṣuṇī should eat at an improper time, it is a pāyattika.

"If a bhikṣuṇī, without having received food, places it in her mouth and swallows it, except for water and tooth-sticks, it is a pāyattika."
“If a bhikṣuṇī, knowing that water contains living beings, should use it, it is a pāyattika.
“If a bhikṣuṇī should give food with her own hand to a naked ascetic or to other male or female ascetics, it is a pāyattika.”
"If a bhikṣuṇī goes to view an armed military force in formation, it is a pāyattika.

However, fire and sensual desire are faults; it is said that sensual desire is not a hindering factor.

Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī stays within an army for two nights and observes the troops preparing for battle, views the vanguard flags, or watches the arrayed and dispersed soldiers, it is a *pāyattika*.
“If a bhikṣuṇī, out of anger and displeasure, strikes another bhikṣuṇī, it is a pāyattika.

“If a bhikṣuṇī, knowing that another bhikṣuṇī has committed a grave offense (sthūlātyaya), conceals it, she commits a pāyattika.

The bhikṣuṇīs should say to that bhikṣuṇī:

You should abandon such an evil view.

Dwelling with those of evil views; a novice, dyed robes, handling jewels, washing animals, causing distress, pointing with a finger, and dwelling together with water.

"Do not misrepresent the Blessed One; it is unwholesome to misrepresent the Blessed One.

"You should abandon such an evil view.
When the bhikṣuṇīs speak thus to that śrāmaṇerī, it is well if she abandons this matter;

If she relinquishes it, that is well;

"This is the proper time.

The exceptions are: during the heat of the season, when ill, while working, while traveling, during a windstorm, during rain, or during both wind and rain; these are the appropriate times.
"If a bhikṣuṇī should intentionally take the life of an animal, it is a pāyattika.
"If a bhikṣuṇī should intentionally cause annoyance to another bhikṣuṇī, even for a moment, with the intent that she find no pleasure therein, it is a pāyattika."
"If a bhikṣuṇī, moreover, tickles another with her fingers, it is a pāyattika.

"If again a bhikṣuṇī, out of anger, knowing that another bhikṣuṇī is pure and without offense, should defame her with a groundless *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offense, it is a *pāyattika*."
"If a bhikṣuṇī should travel along the same road with a man, without another woman present, even for the distance of a single village, it is a pāyattika."
"If a bhikṣuṇī travels along the same road as a caravan of bandits, even for the distance of a single village, it is a pāyattika.

"If a bhikṣuṇī has been invited for four months, she may accept it when necessary.
If she accepts it beyond that period, except during other [permitted] times, it is a pāyattika."
The exceptions are as follows: an individual invitation, a repeated invitation, an earnest invitation, and a regular invitation;
these are the appropriate times. Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī hears other bhikṣuṇīs say:

"Virtuous one, you should now train in such rules of training. He replies:

If a bhikṣuṇī truly desires to seek that [teaching], she should inquire of one learned in the Tripiṭaka; this is the proper occasion.

If one acts with this as the cause, it is a *pāyattika*.

The seventh summary verse says:
Disrespect, drinking alcohol, entering a village, going to another family,

These seven principles for settling disputes are recited every half-month within the Prātimokṣa Sūtra.
The summary verse says:
"Face-to-face and recollection, non-delusion and seeking confession, the majority decision and self-accusation, and the 'covering over with grass'—these settle communal disputes.
One should grant the face-to-face *vinaya*; one ought to grant the face-to-face *vinaya*."
If the *smṛtivinaya* should be granted, the *smṛtivinaya* shall be granted.
If the *amūḍhavinaya* should be granted, the *amūḍhavinaya* shall be granted.
When the Vinaya for seeking the nature of the offense should be granted, the Vinaya for seeking the nature of the offense shall be granted.
When the Vinaya of the majority should be granted, the Vinaya of the majority shall be granted.
One who should be granted the *prātimokṣa* (self-accusation) of the Vinaya should be granted the *prātimokṣa* of the Vinaya;
one who should be granted the *tṛṇaprastāraka* (covering with grass) of the Vinaya should be granted the *tṛṇaprastāraka* of the Vinaya.
"If a dispute arises, it should be settled in accordance with the Teacher’s instruction by means of these seven methods, in conformity with the Dharma and the Vinaya.
'Venerable sirs!
I have now explained the seven principles for settling disputes.'"
Now I ask the venerable ones:
"Are you pure in this matter?
Thus it is asked three times: "Venerable ones!"
"In this matter, we are pure; because we remain silent, I now hold it to be so.

I have recited the eight *pārājika* rules, the twenty *saṃghāvaśeṣa* rules, the thirty-three *naiḥsargika-pāyattika* rules, the one hundred and eighty *pāyattika* rules, the eleven *pratideśanīya* rules, the *śaikṣa* rules, and the seven *adhikaraṇa-śamatha* rules. These are what has been spoken of and included within the Prātimokṣa Sūtra by the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha."

You, sirs, should assemble together in joy and without dispute; with one mind and one voice, like water mixed with milk, you should diligently illuminate and manifest the holy teaching of the Great Master, causing it to abide in peace and happiness. Do not be negligent; you should practice and study accordingly.
"Patience is the highest austerity; it can attain the state of Nirvana.
One who causes affliction to others while claiming to have left the household life is not called a śramaṇa.
This is the precept scripture spoken by the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Vipaśyin.
As one with clear vision avoids dangerous paths and can reach a place of safety,
so the wise person within the realm of birth can distance themselves from all evils.
This is the Sūtra of Precepts spoken by the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śikhin.
Neither disparaging nor harming, Guarding the Sūtra of Precepts well;
Knowing moderation in food and drink, Using humble bedding and seats;
Diligently cultivating superior concentration— This is the teaching of all Buddhas.
This is the precept scripture spoken by the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Viśvabhū:
"Just as a bee gathers from flowers, taking its nectar without harming their color or fragrance;
so should one go among the families."
Do not oppose others; do not look at what they have done or left undone, but examine only your own conduct—whether it is right or wrong.
This is the Sūtra on the Precepts spoken by the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Krakucchanda.
Do not become attached to the concentrated mind; diligently cultivate the place of tranquility.
Being able to provide protection brings freedom from sorrow, and it ensures that mindfulness is never lost.
If a person can practice generosity, their merit increases and enmity naturally subsides.
Cultivating goodness to eliminate all evils, and with delusions exhausted, one reaches Nirvana.
This is the Sūtra of Precepts spoken by the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Kanakamuni.
Commit no evil whatsoever; cultivate all that is wholesome;
thoroughly discipline your own mind—this is the teaching of the Buddhas.
This is the precept scripture spoken by the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Kāśyapa.
To guard the body is excellent;
to guard speech is also good;
to guard the mind is excellent.
To guard everything is most excellent;
a bhikṣu who guards all can liberate himself from all suffering.
He should well guard his speech and also well guard his mind.
Not committing any evil with the body, Always purifying the three types of action;
This is how one can follow The path practiced by the Great Sage.
This is the Sūtra of Precepts spoken by the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śākyamuni.
Vipaśyin, Śikhin, Viśvabhū, Krakucchanda,
Kanakamuni, Kāśyapa, and the Honored One Śākyamuni—
such are the Gods among Gods, the Unsurpassed Tamer of Men.
The seven Buddhas were all heroic and powerful, Able to rescue and protect the world;
Possessing great renown, They all proclaimed this Dharma of the precepts.
All Buddhas and their disciples Together revere and honor the precepts.
By revering the Sūtras on the Precepts, one attains the unsurpassed fruit.
You should seek liberation and diligently practice the Buddha’s teaching;
subdue the army of birth and death as an elephant destroys a thatched hut.
Within this Dharma and Vinaya, by always practicing heedfulness, one can exhaust the ocean of afflictions and reach the end of suffering.
For this purpose, the Sūtra of Precepts is recited; together we shall perform the Poṣadha ceremony.
We should all together revere the precepts, Just as a yak loves its tail.
I have now recited the Sūtra of the Precepts; The Saṃgha has completed the Poṣadha ceremony.
May this merit and benefit all sentient beings, And may they all together attain the Buddha-way.
